CYP2D6_poor_metabolizer.guidance: Avoid codeine and tramadol due to lack of active metabolite conversion (loss of analgesic efficacy). Avoid CYP2D6-metabolized beta-blockers like metoprolol due to 300-500% AUC drug accumulation and risk of severe symptomatic bradycardia. Select non-CYP2D6 alternatives such as Amlodipine (CYP3A4 clearance) or Lisinopril (unchanged renal elimination).
CYP2D6_poor_metabolizer.source: CPIC Guideline for CYP2D6 and Codeine / CYP2D6 Substrates (CPIC-CYP2D6-v3)

CYP2D6_ultrarapid_metabolizer.guidance: Avoid codeine and tramadol due to ultra-rapid conversion to active morphine/metabolites, risking life-threatening respiratory depression and serotonin syndrome. Use non-CYP2D6 opioid or non-opioid analgesics.
CYP2D6_ultrarapid_metabolizer.source: CPIC Guideline for Codeine and CYP2D6 (CPIC-CYP2D6-CODEINE-2021)

CYP2C19_rapid_metabolizer.guidance: Ultra-rapid prodrug activation of Clopidogrel increases systemic active metabolite exposure and bleeding risk. CPIC recommends selecting direct-acting P2Y12 inhibitors such as Ticagrelor (90mg BID) or Prasugrel (10mg QD) that do not depend on CYP2C19 bioactivation.
CYP2C19_rapid_metabolizer.source: CPIC Guideline for CYP2C19 and Clopidogrel Therapy (CPIC-CYP2C19-CLOPIDOGREL-2022)

CYP2C19_poor_metabolizer.guidance: Severely reduced bioactivation of clopidogrel to its active metabolite leads to high risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and stent thrombosis. Switch to Ticagrelor or Prasugrel.
CYP2C19_poor_metabolizer.source: CPIC Guideline for CYP2C19 and Antiplatelet Therapy (CPIC-CYP2C19-ANTIPLATELET-2022)

CYP2C9_slow_metabolizer.guidance: Severely impaired CYP2C9 metabolic clearance leads to 200-400% longer plasma half-life for Warfarin and Celecoxib, risking supratherapeutic INR and severe hemorrhage. Reduce initial Warfarin dose by 50-80% or switch to Direct Oral Anticoagulants (Apixaban 5mg BID or Rivaroxaban) eliminating INR instability.
CYP2C9_slow_metabolizer.source: CPIC Guideline for CYP2C9 and Warfarin / NSAIDs (CPIC-CYP2C9-WARFARIN-2020)

TPMT_poor_metabolizer.guidance: Complete absence of thiopurine S-methyltransferase activity leads to toxic accumulation of thioguanine nucleotides and fatal bone marrow suppression. Reduce thiopurine dosage by 90% or select alternative non-thiopurine immunosuppressive agents (e.g. Methotrexate, Biologics).
TPMT_poor_metabolizer.source: CPIC Guideline for Thiopurine Methyltransferase and Thiopurines (CPIC-TPMT-2018)

SLCO1B1_decreased_function.guidance: Impaired hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1 causes elevated systemic statin concentrations, increasing risk of severe myopathy and rhabdomyolysis by 4-5x with Simvastatin 40-80mg. Switch to low-dose Rosuvastatin (5-10mg) or Pravastatin which do not rely on SLCO1B1 uptake.
SLCO1B1_decreased_function.source: CPIC Guideline for SLCO1B1 and Statin-Induced Myopathy (CPIC-SLCO1B1-STATIN-2022)

HLA-B_5701_positive.guidance: High risk of life-threatening immunologically-mediated hypersensitivity reaction (fever, rash, GI symptoms, respiratory distress). Abacavir is STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED. Select alternative nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors such as Tenofovir disoproxil / Emtricitabine.
HLA-B_5701_positive.source: CPIC Guideline for HLA-B and Abacavir Hypersensitivity (CPIC-HLAB-ABACAVIR-2014)

CYP2D6_normal_metabolizer.guidance: Normal functional metabolic activity confirmed. Standard guideline-directed drug selection and dosing protocols apply.
CYP2D6_normal_metabolizer.source: CPIC Guideline for Wildtype Standard Dosing (CPIC-WILDTYPE-2022)
